headline: Medium prompt-injection and cascading-error risk from Pipecat-to-Rasa handoff; shared-bus concurrency also creates moderate leakage/conflict exposure.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Pipecat can ingest and emit text/voice over a shared bus, and Rasa consumes conversational text/voice through chat channels. That creates a plausible default path where Pipecat output becomes Rasa input, so attacker-controlled content can be treated as instructions. The interaction is inferred from docs-only profiles, so uncertainty pushes severity up.
conditions: IF Pipecat output is forwarded into a Rasa channel without sanitization, injection is possible.
IF the shared bus carries user-authored content between agents, prompt-like payloads can traverse the pair.
mitigations: Add a strict content separator between agent outputs and agent prompts.
Strip or escape instruction-like markup before handing Pipecat text to Rasa.
Route only structured fields, not raw transcripts, across the bus.
requires-engineering: add provenance tags and parser hardening.
requires-engineering: add allowlisted message schemas for inter-agent handoff.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Pipecat touches audio, video, images, text, and conversation state, while Rasa touches text and voice. Both have allowlisted network egress, so shared conversational data can flow into external services in default deployments. The profiles do not prove a shared filesystem, but the shared-bus model and API integrations make leakage plausible enough for medium severity.
conditions: IF either agent forwards transcripts or media to third-party APIs, sensitive content can leave the pair.
IF the shared bus carries conversation state across both agents, data can be exposed to both outputs.
mitigations: Minimize payloads before cross-agent forwarding.
Disable external API connectors for nonessential turns.
Redact PII from transcripts before Rasa receives them.
requires-engineering: enforce per-field data-loss-prevention filters.
requires-engineering: isolate the agents into separate trust zones.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Pipecat supports multiple instances with shared bus state, while Rasa does not support multiple instances. That mismatch suggests contention over shared mutable conversation state or orchestration resources, even though unrestricted filesystem writes are not documented. Because the exact coordination mechanism is unclear, uncertainty escalates to medium rather than low.
conditions: IF both agents write to the same shared conversation state, updates can race.
IF the orchestrator reuses one Rasa instance for multiple Pipecat sessions, state collisions can occur.
mitigations: Serialize writes to shared conversation state.
Assign one session ID per agent pair.
Avoid concurrent mutation of the same memory store.
requires-engineering: add locking around shared mutable resources.
requires-engineering: shard sessions across isolated workers.

D_cascading_error.rationale: Pipecat is a real-time voice framework and Rasa is a dialogue system, so Pipecat output can plausibly become Rasa input with little verification. That makes downstream misrecognition or hallucinated text propagate into the support bot’s responses. The pairwise pathway is inferred from docs-only profiles, so I choose medium and not low.
conditions: IF Rasa treats Pipecat transcripts as authoritative, transcription errors will cascade.
IF Pipecat-generated summaries are used as Rasa training or runtime context, mistakes propagate.
mitigations: Insert a human or rule-based verification step before Rasa acts.
Pass confidence scores alongside transcripts.
Reject low-confidence ASR segments.
requires-engineering: add source-attribution and validation checks.
requires-engineering: separate generation from action-taking.

E_compliance.rationale: Both profiles are open-source and only document generic text/voice handling plus allowlisted egress; no residency, certification, or retention mismatch is evidenced. The only concrete compliance concern is that Pipecat touches richer media classes than Rasa, but the profiles do not show a regulated-data pathway. I therefore keep this low and cite both profiles for the documented gap.
conditions: IF regulated data such as PHI or EU PII is routed through both agents, compliance review is required.
IF one agent logs transcripts longer than the other, retention mismatch becomes relevant.
mitigations: Confirm what data classes are actually routed.
Disable logging for regulated conversations.
Document retention settings for both agents.
requires-engineering: add residency and retention controls.
requires-engineering: map each connector to a compliance owner.
